name: Product Development Lifecycle
description: A six-stage development lifecycle spanning product definition through operations. Each of AWS AI-DLC's three phases is split into parallel product and builder lenses, so every stage has a single accountable role while the two lenses within a phase can proceed together.

phases.name: Product Definition
phases.description: Discovery through baseline handoff: establishes product vision, requirements, experience, and the approved Product Baseline the builder consumes. Governed in detail by the pdlc specification's seven-stage Product Definition Lifecycle.
phases.humanRole: Product person owns and approves every sub-stage; reviewers (design, QA, docs, localization, security, executive) participate at gates

subStages.name: Discovery
subStages.description: Why build this, and is it worth building? Opportunity spec, market analysis, personas, evidence.

subStages.name: Definition
subStages.description: What are we building, for whom, and how do we describe it? MRD/PRD/UXD, requirement registry, GTM narrative.

subStages.name: Experience & Prototype
subStages.description: What does it feel like, and does the definition hold together end-to-end? Runnable static prototype, acceptance journeys.

subStages.name: API
subStages.description: What is the product's programmable contract? Advisory-draft OpenAPI specification the builder may refine.

subStages.name: Documentation
subStages.description: How do users and administrators succeed? User and admin guides, written against the prototype.

subStages.name: Localization
subStages.description: Does it work globally? Guides translated first, then UI string catalogs, then l10n coverage judged.

subStages.name: Baseline & Handoff
subStages.description: Freeze what was approved; hand it to the builder. Reconciled execution spec, Product Baseline manifest, export package.

deliverables.name: Product Baseline
deliverables.description: Revision-pinned, approved manifest handed to the builder

deliverables.name: Requirement Registry
deliverables.description: Immutable requirement IDs with structured acceptance criteria

deliverables.name: Runnable Prototype
deliverables.description: Executable specification of the experience; proves the definition is coherent

deliverables.name: OpenAPI Draft
deliverables.description: Advisory-draft programmable contract; refined into the authoritative contract during Builder Definition

deliverables.name: User and Admin Guides
deliverables.description: Source-locale guides written against the prototype

gates.name: Baseline Approval
gates.description: Readiness report green for the declared profile, no unresolved error-severity findings, baseline approved and revision-pinned

phases.name: Builder Definition
phases.description: Consumes the approved Product Baseline and produces the authoritative technical design: requirements translation, architecture, and the finalized API contract.
phases.humanRole: Builder person (engineer, AI coding agent) owns; technical lead / architecture review approves

deliverables.name: Technical Requirements (TRD/IRD)
deliverables.description: Translates the Product Baseline into technical requirements, architecture, and data models

deliverables.name: API Contract
deliverables.description: Refines Product Definition's advisory OpenAPI draft into the finalized, authoritative technical contract

deliverables.name: Reference SDK Client
deliverables.description: Auto-generated client library from the finalized API contract; used as a reference implementation and for acceptance testing. Advisory — proves the contract is implementable and testable, not itself a requirement, mirroring how Product Definition's prototype is advisory evidence for the PRD/UXD.

gates.name: Technical Design Review
gates.description: Technical design is feasible, API contract finalized, risks identified and mitigation planned

phases.name: Implementation
phases.description: Code is written against the Builder Definition technical contract.
phases.securityOverlayNote: Application Security Posture Management domains 1-5 (git posture, code security, secret/PII scan, open source security, SBOM) overlay this stage. The overlay is defined and owned by consuming security-analysis tooling (e.g. Threat Model Spec), not by this framework.

deliverables.name: Source Code
deliverables.description: Implementation against the finalized technical contract

deliverables.name: SBOM
deliverables.description: Software bill of materials generated at build

gates.name: Code Review / CI Gate
gates.description: Automated checks (build, lint, test, SAST/SCA) plus human code review

phases.name: Deployment
phases.description: Built artifacts are released to target environments.
phases.securityOverlayNote: ASPM domains 6-9 (IaC scan, CI/CD posture, container security, artifact security) overlay this stage. The overlay is defined and owned by consuming security-analysis tooling, not by this framework.

gates.name: Release Gate
gates.description: Deployment validation, rollback readiness, release approval

phases.name: Builder Operations
phases.description: Infrastructure, security, and reliability operations for the deployed system: monitoring, incident response, cloud security posture. Runs concurrently with Product Operations, not sequentially after it.
phases.securityOverlayNote: ASPM domain 10 (cloud context) overlays this stage, alongside dynamic testing (DAST, penetration testing, red teaming) which is not an ASPM domain. The overlay is defined and owned by consuming security-analysis tooling, not by this framework.

phases.name: Product Operations
phases.description: Adoption, usage, and feedback operations for the shipped product: activation, retention, feature usage, PMF signal, and customer feedback synthesis that feeds the next Product Definition baseline revision. Runs concurrently with Builder Operations, not sequentially after it.
phases.humanRole: Product person owns; drift and adoption signal reviewed against the current baseline

deliverables.name: Adoption Report
deliverables.description: Activation, feature usage, and adoption metrics against the Product Baseline's success criteria

deliverables.name: Feedback Synthesis
deliverables.description: Customer feedback reconciled against the current baseline (drift detection)

gates.name: Baseline Revision Trigger
gates.description: Significant drift between the approved definition and shipped/observed reality triggers a new Product Definition baseline revision

dependencies.description: Phase dependency graph. Operations phases feed back into Product Definition, closing the lifecycle rather than terminating it.

integrations: Threat Model Spec (ASPM security-posture overlay on the builder stages; tms analyze command)
VisionSpec / VisionStudio (tags each spec type with its PDLC stage for spec-driven analysis; initiative, phase, and RMI tracking against PDLC-staged work)

relatedFrameworks.relationship: PDLC splits each AWS AI-DLC phase into parallel product and builder lenses: Inception into Product Definition + Builder Definition, Construction into Implementation + Deployment, Operation into Builder Operations + Product Operations (the last pair runs concurrently, not sequentially).

references.title: AWS AI-Driven Development Lifecycle
references.note: PDLC's phase-to-lens split is defined relative to this three-phase model
